note: Design elements are decisions with a specification: a format, an algorithm, a protocol, a schema. Requirements trace to them many-to-one. A requirement with no design element must be explicitly classified instead, so the absence is deliberate rather than an oversight. The chain is: release-notes promise -> requirement -> design element -> test.

elements.title: Action record schema
elements.decides: Which fields constitute an action record, their types, and what is deliberately excluded (no prompt, no conversation, no model output).

elements.title: Canonical encoding
elements.decides: Deterministic serialisation: recursive key ordering, array order preserved, number and null handling, and the rule that every field at every depth contributes to the digest.

elements.title: Leaf and salt construction
elements.decides: Salt length and source, leaf = H(salt || canonical), and where salts are stored so a disclosure can carry one without revealing others.

elements.title: Chain construction
elements.decides: h_i = H(h_(i-1) || leaf_i), the genesis value, sequence semantics, and what a verifier may conclude from a break.

elements.title: Batching and Merkle tree
elements.decides: Batch boundaries, tree shape, odd-leaf handling, and root computation — the construction that lets one action be disclosed without the rest.

elements.title: Key hierarchy, signing and epoch ratchet
elements.decides: What an epoch is, how the signing key evolves, how the predecessor is destroyed, the KMS and HSM integration surface, and recovery after compromise.

elements.title: Checkpoint format
elements.decides: The C2SP tlog-witness conformant checkpoint, its signed preimage, and how the operator identity and sequence appear in it.

elements.title: Witness protocol
elements.decides: Submission and response, enrolment, per-operator sequence enforcement, countersignature contents, tree-head publication, key rotation, and every failure mode.

elements.title: Policy files
elements.decides: Two separate schemas: the collector's witness set, and the verifier's acceptance policy. Plus how a policy change is recorded as a chain event.

elements.title: Coverage model
elements.decides: Heartbeat cadence and contents, the build digest, gap declaration semantics, and precisely what the claim "100% captured between T1 and T2" asserts.

elements.title: Evidence pack format
elements.decides: The artifact an auditor receives: records, salts, inclusion paths, every countersignature collected, and the public keys needed to check them.

elements.title: Verification algorithm
elements.decides: The ordered checks, the verdict taxonomy including an inconclusive outcome, and what each distinct failure permits a reader to conclude.

elements.title: Storage and erasure
elements.decides: The content store, pointer scheme, crypto-shredding procedure, and how retention is configured without touching the cryptography.

elements.title: Collector architecture
elements.decides: The shared capture core, the OMA backend, the MCP proxy, and where the capture boundary sits in each.

elements.title: Failure and availability model
elements.decides: Fail-open behaviour, the durable queue, retry and backoff, late countersignature handling, and the guarantee that the collector can never block a run.

elements.title: Format versioning and algorithm agility
elements.decides: Version negotiation in the record and pack, and the migration path when a hash or signature algorithm must change.

elements.title: Release and provenance pipeline
elements.decides: Build reproducibility, provenance attestation, release signing, SBOM generation, and how a heartbeat's build digest is traced back to source.

elements.title: Witness practice statement structure
elements.decides: What the countersignature asserts and disclaims, how the statement is versioned and anchored, and how the time discipline is declared.
